title: Mode-selective electron-phonon coupling drives charge density waves in the kagome metals YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$
authors: Wenqian Tu, Run Lv, Dingfu Shao, Yuping Sun, Wenjian Lu
abstract: YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$ host the highest charge density wave (CDW) transition temperatures ever reported in kagome metals, $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}\approx 800$ and 400~K, with propagation vectors $Q_{\mathrm{CDW}}\approx(1/2,0,0)$ and $(1/4,0,0)$, respectively. The microscopic mechanism behind these record values has remained unresolved. Here, we combine anharmonic phonon renormalization extracted from molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learned force field with mode-resolved electron-phonon coupling (EPC) analysis to identify this mechanism. The CDW is driven by mode-selective EPC: the Ru out-of-plane phonon modes couple the Ru-$d_{xz}/d_{yz}$ and Si-$p_x/p_y$ orbitals, and the phonon linewidth peaks sharply at $Q_{\mathrm{CDW}}$, while the featureless electronic susceptibility rules out Fermi-surface nesting. Phonon anharmonicity melts the CDW, and the anharmonic phonon spectra reproduce both $Q_{\mathrm{CDW}}$ and $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$ in good agreement with experiments. Molecular dynamics simulations also visualize the CDW melting in real space. Chemical bonding analysis further shows that the smaller Y$^{3+}$ radius strengthens the Ru-Ru bonds, enhancing lattice rigidity and accounting for the factor-of-two higher $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$ of YRu$_3$Si$_2$. Our results establish a unified microscopic picture of CDW formation and melting in kagome metals YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$.
summary: This work establishes a unified microscopic picture for CDW formation in kagome metals YRu3Si2 and LaRu3Si2. The research demonstrates that the CDW instability is driven by mode-selective electron-phonon coupling, not Fermi surface nesting. Furthermore, it explains the large difference in transition temperatures by linking it to enhanced lattice rigidity controlled by the A-site cation size.
main_problem: To resolve the microscopic mechanism driving the record-high Charge Density Wave (CDW) transition temperatures in kagome metals YRu3Si2 and LaRu3Si2.
main_result: The CDW is driven by mode-selective electron-phonon coupling (EPC) involving Ru-d and Si-p orbitals, and the high transition temperature is enhanced by lattice rigidity stemming from the smaller Y3+ ion.
method: The study combines mode-resolved EPC analysis, anharmonic phonon calculations via Molecular Dynamics (MD) using MLFF, and electronic susceptibility analysis to rule out Fermi surface nesting.
model_or_system: The system consists of the kagome metals YRu3Si2 and LaRu3Si2, whose electronic and lattice dynamics are modeled using DFT and advanced simulation techniques.
key_observables: Electron linewidth ($\Gamma_{nk}$), momentum-resolved phonon linewidth ($\gamma(\mathbf{q})$), electronic susceptibility ($\chi(\mathbf{q})$), and CDW formation energy ($\Delta E$).
important_parameters: High CDW transition temperatures ($\approx 800$ K for YRu3Si2), specific CDW propagation vectors, and the ionic radius of the A-site cation (Y vs La).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Migdal approximation for EPC and assumes that anharmonic phonon renormalization governs the CDW melting process.
figures_summary: Figures show crystal structures, orbital-projected band structures, electron linewidth distributions, and phonon spectra comparing harmonic and anharmonic regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the high-temperature CDW state, then using EPC analysis to pinpoint the coupling mechanism, ruling out alternative theories like FSN, and finally using MD simulations and bonding analysis to explain the temperature and material dependence of the CDW.
why_interesting: The detailed coupling between lattice vibrations (phonons) and electronic degrees of freedom (electrons) to drive a collective electronic state (CDW) is a core topic in strongly correlated electron physics, relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Side and top views of the YRu3Si2 and LaRu3Si2 crystal structures showing the kagome Ru layer (pink), Si layers (blue), and Y/La cations (green). (b) Orbital-projected band structure and (c) electron linewidth distribution of YRu3Si2. (d) Brillouin zone with high-symmetry points labeled. (e) Orbital-projected band structure and (f) electron linewidth distribution of LaRu3Si2.

FIG. 2. (a) Harmonic phonon spectrum (dashed line) and temperature-dependent anharmonic phonon spectra (colored solid lines) for the high-temperature P6/mmm phase of YRu3Si2. (b) Phonon dispersion of YRu3Si2 at 700 K, color-weighted by the contributions from Y, Ru, and Si atomic vibrations. The Eliashberg spectral function α2F(ω) (blue) and the integrated EPC constant λ (red) are plotted on the right side. (c), (d) Same as (a), (b) for LaRu3Si2 at 400 K.

FIG. 3. (a) Phonon linewidth γ(q) of the lowest phonon mode for YRu3Si2. (b) Real part χ′(q) and (c) imaginary part χ′′(q) of the electronic susceptibility for YRu3Si2, where QCDW is indicated by a black arrow. (d)–(f) Corresponding results for LaRu3Si2. All panels display the quantities in the Qz = 1/2 plane.

FIG. 4. MLFF-driven molecular dynamics simulations of the CDW melting process. (a) YRu3Si2 at 10 K, 400 K, and 800 K. (b) LaRu3Si2 at 10 K, 250 K, and 500 K. Black arrows indicate the Ru displacement directions relative to the high-symmetry positions, and pink lines mark the Ru-Ru bonds shortened by the CDW distortion, whose number progressively decreases with increasing temperature.

FIG. 5. COHP analysis of the parent P6/mmm and CDW-distorted supercells. (a) YRu3Si2 parent, (b) YRu3Si2 CDW, (c) LaRu3Si2 parent, (d) LaRu3Si2 CDW. The curves show the COHP of the Ru-Ru, Y-Si (La-Si), and Ru-Si bonding pairs, and the numbers denote the corresponding ICOHP values.
